For ages, I’ve been wanting to tell my stories around a specific place in OSM. Not specifically a “review” of a business, but simply a personal anecdote about me and that particular place. Years ago, I received my first invitation to give a talk about OSM. On that occasion, I proposed this project: “What if we create a platform where people can share their personal stories around a specific place?” But I was probably just an “idea guy” back then. My programming skills weren’t developed enough to build the platform all by myself, and I had no idea how to get funding to pay for a hosting service anyway. So I shelved the idea for a long time. Fast-forward to 2026, I eventually thought to myself: maybe it’s finally the right time to revisit that old dream. So I built this. First, you log in using your OSM account. I want this platform to be somewhat of an extension of OSM Diary. Here, you can not only write an “OSM Diary” entry associated with your OSM account, but also link it to a specific place. Every story is tied to a particular location. If a place is significant enough that many people have posted their stories about it, you can see all the other stories associated with that place. pages.text: RSS Feed (Really Simple Syndication) - BBC Sport Published 22 May 2024 What is RSS? In a world heaving under the weight of billions of web pages, keeping up to date with the information you want can be a drag. Wouldn't it be better to have the latest news and features delivered directly to you, rather than clicking from site to site? Using RSS (Really Simple Syndication) allows you to see when sites from all over the internet have added new content. You can get the latest headlines and articles (or even audio files, photographs or video) in one place, as soon as they are published, without having to remember to visit each site every day. RSS takes the hassle out of staying up-to-date, by showing you the very latest information that you are interested in. RSS feeds are just a special kind of web page, designed to be read by computers rather than people. It might help to think of them as the free, internet version of the old-fashioned ticker-tape news wire machines. Not all websites currently provide RSS and not all sections of the BBC or BBC Sport website are available as feeds. How do I start using RSS feeds? In general, the first thing you need is something called a news reader. This is a piece of software that checks RSS feeds and lets you read any new articles that have been added to them. There are many different versions, some of which are accessed using a browser, and some of which are downloadable applications. Close Rub21's Diary A map of open OSM notes, sorted by what they need Posted by Rub21 on 12 November 2026 in English . There are about 450,000 open notes on OpenStreetMap. Each one is a message from someone who saw a problem on the map. But to know what a note needs, you have to open it and read it, one by one. That takes a lot of time. So I trained a machine learning model to do this first read for us. I also made a simple website to show the results: → https://osm-notes.rub21.com What does the model do? The model reads the first comment of each note and gives it two labels: Category : what the mapper should do. For example: missing place, place closed or changed, wrong name, missing or wrong road, other wrong data, spam, empty, or not mappable (opinions, questions). Theme : what the note is about. For example: food, shops, health, roads, transport. How I built it The notes. Andrés ( AngocA ) built OSM-Notes-Ingestion . It loads all OSM notes into a database and keeps them up to date every minute. On top of it, I built a small pipeline that: loads the full notes dump from the planet file, takes the first comment of each note (the one that explains the problem), detects the language of each note. Training data. This was the hardest part, and it took several rounds. The AI helped me a lot, but I reviewed many of its labels: I sent about 10,000 notes to three popular AI models: Claude, GPT and Gemini. The data team at Mapbox have built tools that allow detecting and cleaning these issues as they happen on the map. Detecting issues with OSMlint To detect issues, we run spatial analysis on the map data of the whole world everyday using OSMlint . This is made possible be leveraging the power of tile-reduce to analyze OpenStreetMap vector tiles using javascript. OSMlint consists of a set of validators which check the data on each tile for common issues in geometry and tags. An example validator is crossingHighways which detects roads that cross each other without an intersection. Each validator produces a GeoJSON output of the OpenStreetMap geometries that are invalid and needs review. Fixing issues with To-fix To-fix is a micro tasking tool that helps us create tasks of issues to fix on OpenStreetMap. The issues collected with OSMlint is loaded into to-fix, each of which is then reviewed by a member of the mapping community or the Mapbox data team. Over 500,000 issues have been fixed so far using to-fix. To-fix also allows marking issues as false positives. These are later investigated and used to improve the validator algorithm in OSMlint. The linting pipeline We’ve implemented an architecture that automates the detection of issues using OSMlint and loading them into to-fix on a daily basis. January 17, 2025 Rubella Symptoms and Complications Key points Most children and adults who get rubella usually have mild illness with a rash starting on the face. Up to 70% of women who get rubella may experience arthritis. The most serious complication from rubella infection is the harm it can cause a developing baby. Signs and symptoms Rubella is usually mild, with few noticeable symptoms. In children For children who do have symptoms, a red rash is typically the first sign. The rash generally first appears on the face and then spreads to the rest of the body, lasting about 3 days. Other symptoms that may occur 1 to 5 days before the rash appears include: Low-grade fever Headache Mild pink eye (redness or swelling of the white of the eye) General discomfort Swollen and enlarged lymph nodes Cough Runny nose In adults Most adults who get rubella usually have a mild illness, with: Low-grade fever Sore throat A rash that starts on the face and spreads to the rest of the body Some adults may also have a headache, pink eye, and general discomfort before the rash appears. Introduction The best way to protect against rubella is to get the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. Children may get the measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella (MMRV) vaccine instead, which protects against chickenpox too. Or they can get the chickenpox vaccine separately. Most people who are vaccinated with MMR & MMRV will be protected for life. Vaccines and high rates of vaccination have made these diseases much less common in the United States. On the way home, my right arm basically stopped working, so really weird symptoms," Lawes said. "Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement. It added that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." pages.text: Ryan Crowley: Airman's rugby career has taken off at Leicester Tigers - BBC Sport Image source, Shutterstock Image caption, Ryan Crowley has scored two tries in 10 matches for Leicester Tigers By Andrew Aloia BBC Sport, East Midlands Published 18 November 2026 Corporal Ryan Crowley has spent a decade helping get aircraft off the ground. It has taken just as long for the winger to finally get his professional rugby union career to take off. It was only a year ago that Crowley was plucked from his role as an avionics engineer with the Royal Air Force and recruited by Leicester Tigers. The 28-year-old Welshman was handed a deal with the giants of the game, the 11-time Prem champions - when he didn't even know one was up for grabs. "I thought I got sent up to Tigers to go and get experience and do a pre-season with a pro team," he told BBC Sport. The military man had simply followed orders. Chinnor, the second division side he was playing for, asked him to join Geoff Parling's Tigers for the early weeks of their Prem Rugby Cup campaign last season. "After a couple of weeks Geoff said, 'you've been successful in your trial', and I was like, 'what trial?'," Crowley added. "The silver lining to not knowing it was a trial is I had no pressure on me; I just came up and I was just trying to learn as much as I could. He focuses on the national security side of the Justice beat, including counterterrorism, counterintelligence and transnational repression. Before joining NPR, Lucas worked for a decade as a foreign correspondent for The Associated Press based in Poland, Egypt and Lebanon. In Poland, he covered the fallout from the revelations about secret CIA prisons in Eastern Europe. In the Middle East, he reported on the ouster of Hosni Mubarak in 2011 and the turmoil that followed. He also covered the Libyan civil war, the Syrian conflict and the rise of the Islamic State. He reported from Iraq during the U.S. occupation and later during the Islamic State takeover of Mosul in 2014. He also covered intelligence and national security for Congressional Quarterly. That said, planning is an important step in being prepared and ready for your adventure. Remember, the Monument can be very unforgiving, and its wild character should not be underestimated. And although overnight stays on the monument do not require a permit, free permits are available at any of the local Visitor Centers and are highly encouraged. The permit system can become crucial in the case of a search and rescue . Below are some best practices to keep in mind when recreating on the GSENM: It’s always a good idea to let people know your itinerary and when you expect be back Travel in groups rather than by yourself Before beginning any of your Monument adventures, make sure you've planned your way in, and planned your way out Know the extended weather forecast Carry extra clothing, blankets, food and water for emergencies Remember, cell phone coverage across the Monument is sparse if at all Plan Ahead and Prepare

The Safford Field Office—whose boundaries stretch from the Navajo Nation in the north to the international boundary with Mexico in the south—is responsible for stewardship of eight units within BLM’s National Landscape Conservation System, including the Gila Box Riparian National Conservation Area , six wilderness areas, including the world-renowned Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness and one wilderness study area. Public lands in this field office also include 11 Areas of Critical Environmental Concern, Muleshoe Ranch Cooperative Management Area , Black Hills Back Country Byway , Willcox Playa National Natural Landmark , Guadalupe Canyon Outstanding Natural Area, one property on the National Register of Historic Places and more than 30 miles of stream segments under consideration for Wild & Scenic River designation. They assembled a diverse group of habitat specialists and sage-grouse experts from state, federal, and nongovernmental organizations to develop this habitat evaluation tool. In 2006, the “Greater Sage-grouse Comprehensive Conservation Strategy,” published by the Western Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies, highlighted the development and implementation of the HAF. That strategy outlined a number of objectives for the HAF, which included a temporal and spatial method for evaluating sagebrush habitats for sage-grouse suitability at various landscape scales. The HAF is a cornerstone of the habitat monitoring component of the sage-grouse adaptive management strategy. Acarajé da Dinha, a legendary kiosk in Salvador’s Rio Vermelho district, is renowned for its acarajé , a savory fritter made from black-eyed peas and an emblem of Afro-Brazilian culture. The reason is simple to me. The very notion that Cameron Bancroft - the most inexperienced batsman in the Australia team at the time – would use sandpaper on the ball against South Africa without the bowlers knowing has never made sense. It has never seemed remotely plausible to me, as a former bowler, that the bowlers didn't know what was happening in Cape Town in 2018. It just doesn't seem possible. Therefore, this day of reckoning was always going to come. Let's be clear - as long as there has been cricket, there has been ball-tampering. There is no point hiding from the fact. Back in the day it was about shining the ball, maybe using something like a sweet to get a sheen on one side. Reverse swing was a ball-tampering game-changer. There was a requirement for a wearing process, roughing up and drying the ball. But, to get one thing straight, whether a ball is being tampered with or not, it belongs to the bowlers. pages.text: Santander, Spain: A 2027 Guide to Its Waterfront Art Museums | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Beloved by Spaniards, Santander Is Becoming a Global Art Mecca The easygoing beachfront city is getting a host of new and reborn museums. A 2014 transformation by landscape architect Fernando Caruncho more than doubled the size of Pereda Gardens, in the historic heart of Santander. Luis Fonseca, Getty Images By Eddi Fiegel Published October 20, 2026 Santander, a port city in northwestern Spain, has long seduced Spaniards with its spectacular horseshoe bay surrounded by rolling green hills and the Cantabrian mountains in the distance. But now the city, the capital of the Cantabria region, is poised to become an international art destination. In September 2026, the new arts, culture, and technology center Faro Santander opened in a historic building redesigned by acclaimed British architect David Chipperfield with a permanent collection including works by such legendary figures as el Greco, Rubens, Velázquez, and Goya. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) Meanwhile, 2027 will bring the first outpost of Madrid’s renowned Reina Sofía museum. The impressive Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology of Cantabria also has a new home designed by the Barcelona-based architecture practice Mendoza Partida. Art lovers are sure to appreciate the city’s walkable city center—where ornate, neoclassical façades sit alongside Baroque churches and grand, porticoed squares—and the wide sandy beaches lined with elegant fin-de-siècle villas.

pages.text: Sarina Wiegman contract: Why England manager faces biggest challenge yet - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Published 19 October 2026 When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Published 19 October Why must England evolve? Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup.

Learn about applying for programs like TSA Precheck and Global Entry and managing memberships. What are the Trusted Traveler Programs, and how do you apply? The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) manages the Trusted Traveler Programs. These include TSA Precheck and Global Entry . As a pre-approved member, you can use expedited lanes at U.S. airports and when entering the U.S. by land or sea. TSA Precheck is for travelers departing from U.S. airports. Global Entry is for travelers entering the U.S. from international destinations by air, land, or sea. There are also programs for entering the U.S. from Canada and Mexico. To apply, you will need to pay a fee and provide documents proving your identity. Depending on the program, you may need to complete an interview.
